reason: Data Formulator's local web app (pip install data_formulator; python -m data_formulator) starts on CPU and its data loading/workspace features work without any LLM key.
demo: README Get Started, Option 2: pip install data_formulator && python -m data_formulator (web UI at http://localhost:5567)
goal: Install Data Formulator from the cloned repo (or pip) and start the web server with `python -m data_formulator` on port 5567 (frontend must be served at /). Provide /work/env.sh and /work/run.sh that start the server in the background and return once it is ready. No LLM API key is needed; the data upload/workspace API must work: uploading a CSV through POST /api/tables/create-table and reading it back through /api/tables/list-tables, get-table and sample-table.
check: The hidden test checks that the server serves the web UI and app-config, then uploads a generated CSV as a table and verifies it is listed and returns the correct rows and counts.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Oracle's /api/tables/* curl calls omit the X-Workspace-Id header; the backend requires it by design (the frontend always sends it and the workspace is created lazily), so every table call fails on a correct install.
get-table was only substring-checked; v2 also checks total_rows and page length against the source's response fields.
evidence: py-src/data_formulator/workspace_factory.py:120-135 - get_active_workspace_id reads X-Workspace-Id; get_workspace raises 'No active workspace. X-Workspace-Id header is required.'
py-src/data_formulator/workspace_factory.py:137-147 - unknown workspace ids are created on first use
data/runs/microsoft-data-formulator/result.json audit - with the header, create-table returns success and list-tables shows the table
